Use this report to set the next fee: a fee per hour below your target means the next proposal needs more fee, fewer hours or a charge for extra rounds.

Open Start and type your studio name and your own limits in the yellow cells: retainer share, FF&E deposit share, trades mark-up, target margin, hour cost, capacity hours, wanted utilisation, bill days and chase minutes.
Check Team, Billing Rates, Clients and Projects. They hold the people, rates, clients and projects that every other sheet looks up.
Log time on Time Entries every week. Mark time you cannot bill as No. Value, cost and week fill in; Timesheet by Week shows utilisation.
At month-end fill Unbilled Time for each hourly project: billable hours, their value and the invoice that billed them. Use the Time Billing calculator to apply any retainer credit.
Enter every invoice on Client Invoices with its kind, dates and status. Days late, state, open amount and overdue amount fill in by themselves.
Use Payment Schedule for invoices still to come, Fee Milestones for fixed-fee milestones, FF&E Invoices for deposits and balances and Trades Re-billing for contractor mark-up.
Record each payment on Payments Received. Track retainers and what was credited on Retainers.
Work the overdue list: Overdue Chase Log records each reminder and promise, Reminder Rules sets your steps by client kind and Statements by Client ranks who to call.
Write credits and write-offs on Credits and Write-offs, and watch Hours Over Fee and Project Profit to see whether each fee paid for the hours.

Use the 14 calculators for time billing, fixed fee against hours, percentage fees, invoice plans, retainer credit, late payment cost, reminder dates, slow payers, collection priority, utilisation, effective rate and what-ifs.
Read the Billing Dashboard and Charts every week: invoiced, received, overdue, hours, utilisation, unbilled time, retainers and margin per hour.

Vendors with orders, balance and on-time share
One row per vendor on a trade account: category, price level, terms, trade discount, deposit and lead time; orders, order value, share, open balance and on-time share fill in by themselves.
Vendor scorecard with overall score and rank
One row per vendor: your price and communication marks; on-time share, damage rate, the weighted overall score, rank and the check against the target fill in from the orders and the issue log.
Purchase orders by vendor with delay and on-time flag
One row per purchase order: vendor, project, dates, total and status; the days the promise slipped, the delay days, the on-time flag and the balance still open fill in by themselves.
Vendor payments with due date, days late and state
One row per deposit, balance or credit with a vendor: amount, due date and payment date; the days late, the state, the amount still open and the vendor phone fill in by themselves.
Trade accounts with credit headroom and rebate
One row per trade account: credit limit, discount tier, terms, rep and the annual rebate agreement; the used credit, headroom, rebate earned and the gap to the rebate threshold fill in by themselves.
Vendor price lists with discount share and expiry
One row per product line on a vendor trade price list: list price, trade price and valid-until date; the discount share, days to expiry and an expiry check fill in by themselves.
Vendor comparison by category with value score
Three or four vendors per category side by side; discount, lead time and rating come from Vendors, and the value score, category rank and best-value flag fill in by themselves.
Delivery performance by vendor with days late
One row per delivery: vendor, carrier, promised and delivered dates and status; the days late, the on-time flag and the phones for a call fill in by themselves.
Damage and quality issues with credit and days to resolve
One row per damaged, wrong, short or faulty delivery: vendor, kind, resolution and credit; the days to resolve, whether it is still open and the vendor phone fill in by themselves.
Contractors with jobs, quoted against actual and overrun
One row per contractor or trade: day rate, rating and since date; the jobs, the quoted and actual totals, the average overrun, the rework days and the true cost fill in from Trade Jobs.
Trade jobs with quote, actual, overrun and rework
One row per job a contractor does on a project: scope, dates, quote and actual cost; the days, overrun share, true cost with rework and the within-quote check fill in by themselves.
Contractor scorecard with true cost and rank
One row per contractor: your quality, punctuality and communication marks; the price against quote, rework, overall score, rank, true cost and overrun fill in from Trade Jobs.
Contractor availability by week with booked and free days
One row per contractor and week: the days already booked; the free days, a booked flag and the contractor phone fill in by themselves, ready for the next job.
Contractor quotes with status and accepted share
One row per quote asked for: contractor, project, scope, amount and status; the accepted share of that contractor, the days the quote implies at their day rate and the phone fill in by themselves.
Contractor payments with retention and days late
One row per contractor payment: job, amount paid after retention, retention held, due date and payment date; the contractor, days late and state fill in by themselves.
Insurance and licence checks with days to expiry
One row per insurance, licence, certificate or agreement of a contractor or vendor: valid-until and checked-on dates; the days to expiry, the state and the phone fill in by themselves.
Vendor meetings and visits with follow-up
One row per showroom visit, factory visit, call, show meeting, sample review or price review: designer, outcome and follow-up date; the follow-up check and the vendor phone fill in by themselves.
For each room type and category, the first and second choice vendor and the reason; their scores come from the Vendor Scorecard and flag a second choice that now scores higher.
Vendor risks with level, action and review date
One row per vendor risk: kind, level, action, owner and review date; whether it is still open, the days to review and the review check fill in by themselves.
Team with roles, hours, visits and open risks
The owner designer, four staff and seven freelance specialists: role, hours a week, hour cost and bill rate; the margin per hour, vendor visits and open risks owned fill in by themselves.

Hello {contact}, we would like to open a trade account with {name} for {category}. Please send your account form, trade terms and lead times.
Vendor: send your trade price list
Hello {contact}, please send your current trade price list for {category}, with your discount and lead times. Thank you.
Hello, your trade price for {product_line} is valid until {valid_until}. Please send the renewed price list before that date.
Hello {contact}, please confirm in writing our trade discount of {trade_discount} and a lead time of {lead_weeks} weeks for the coming year.
Vendor: a volume discount next year
Hello {rep}, we ordered {year_value} from you this year. Can we agree a volume rebate of {rebate_pct} above {rebate_from} for next year?
Vendor: thank you, delivery on time
Hello, thank you: delivery {delivery_id} for order {po_id} arrived on {delivered_on}, on time. We value it.
Hello, delivery {delivery_id} for order {po_id} was promised for {scheduled_on} and is {days_late} days late. Please explain and give a firm date.
Vendor: a quality issue on an order
Hello, there is a problem on order {po_id}: {kind}, found on {date}. Please confirm a replacement date or a credit.
Hello {party}, our records show your {kind} is valid until {valid_until}. Please send the renewed document.
Hello, we paid {amount} for order {po_id} on {paid_on}. Please confirm that it arrived and send the receipt.
Vendor: a lead time update is needed
Hello, please confirm the delivery date of order {po_id}. We now expect it on {expected_on} and the client is waiting.
Hello {contact}, we may place a larger order in {category} soon. Please reserve stock and tell us the lead time, now {lead_weeks} weeks.
Hello, please quote this work for {project}: {scope}. Send a fixed price, the days and your earliest start date.
Hello, your quote of {quoted} for {scope} on {project} is accepted. Please start on {start_date}.
Hello, are you free to start {scope} on {start_date}? Please tell us how many days you need.
Hello {contact}, please send your current liability insurance and trade certificate. We check them before every job.
Hello, thank you for {scope} on {project}. The job ended on {end_date}. We will send the finishing list and release the payment on the agreed date.
Contractor: a rework item to fix
Hello, a finishing fix is open on {project}, about {rework_days} days of work. Please call us to agree the date of your visit.
Hello, your payment of {amount} is due on {due_date}. We hold {retention} as retention until the finishing fixes are done.
Hello, please confirm your schedule for the week of {week}. We have you booked for {booked_days} days.
Owner: a vendor is below the score
Hello, {vendor} scores {overall}, below the target of {target_score}. On-time share {ontime_share}. Please decide on a review call.
Owner: a vendor share is high
Hello, {vendor} now holds {share} of the order value, {order_value} in total. Please check the concentration of our spend.
Hello, the {kind} of {party} expires on {valid_until}, in {days_to_expiry} days. State: {state}. Please ask for the renewal.
Owner: a contractor is over quote
Hello, {contractor} is over quote on {project}: quoted {quoted}, actual {actual}, overrun {overrun_share}. Please review the extra cost.
Owner: the annual review is ready
Hello, the annual vendor review is ready. {vendor} ranks number {rank} with a score of {overall}. Please open the Vendor Scorecard.
Lead: the preferred vendor for a room
Hello, for {room_type} ({category}) please use {vendor} first, with {second_choice} as the second choice. Reason: {reason}.
Assistant: renew a trade price list
Hello, the trade price list of {vendor} for {product_line} is valid until {valid_until}. Please ask them for the renewed list.
Hello, please check the delivery performance of {vendor}. Delivery {delivery_id} was {days_late} days late. Call them and note the reason.

Dear {col:accounts.rep}, we would like to open or update a trade account with {col:accounts.vendor}. We are an interior design studio that buys furniture, fittings and equipment for our clients.

We ask for the trade price, a discount tier of {col:accounts.discount_tier} ({col:accounts.trade_discount}), payment terms of {col:accounts.terms_days} days and a credit limit of {col:accounts.credit_limit}.
We expect orders of about {col:accounts.year_value} this year and would value a volume rebate of {col:accounts.rebate_pct} above {col:accounts.rebate_from}. Prices are before any tax.
Please send your account form, your trade terms and your current price list.
Dear partner, we review every vendor each year. Your on-time share was {col:scorecard.ontime_share} and your damage and quality rate was {col:scorecard.damage_rate}.
Your overall score is {col:scorecard.overall} against our target of {col:scorecard.target_score}, rank {col:scorecard.rank}. Result: {col:scorecard.verdict}.
We would like to agree how to keep late deliveries and damaged items low, and to confirm your trade discount and lead times for the next year.
Please reply with your plan and a date for a call.
